newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Chess-Donetsk moves clear in World Cities Chess.
newsitem.headline: Chess-Donetsk moves clear in World Cities Chess.

text.p: A crushing win over Rangoon on Sunday has given the Ukrainian city of Donetsk a near decisive lead with only two rounds remaining in the World Cities Chess Championships in Jakarta.
The all-Grandmaster team from Donetsk had little trouble disposing of the lowly ranked Burmese.
Rangoon top player Zaw Win Lay managed a draw against Igor Novikov, the only game which stood between Rangoon and a 0-4 whitewash.
Donetsk's win increased their lead to two points as the pre-tournament favourite Moscow could only managed a narrow 2.5-1.5 victory over third-seeded Tashkent.
Moscow top scorer Sergei Tiviakov was the Russian's only winner on Sunday against the Uzbek.

The only other possible contender for the gold medal and the $10,000 first prize was Oslo, but the Norwegians wlll now have to be content with vying for a minor placing after lowering their colours to the surprising Bandung team. Bandung exploited the lack of depth in the Oslo team, winning on both boards where Oslo was forced to field non-grandmasters.

Sunday's round also saw Sydney move into medal contention after a remarkable 4-0 victory over a higher-ranked Jakarta team, while dark horses Ho Chi Minh City kept their hopes alive with a hard-fought victory over another local team Medan.
The inaugural World Cities Championships, featuring 30 teams from 14 countries, conclude on Monday.
